question_text:
Sydney tower in Australia is the second tallest observation tower in the Southern Hemisphere.
Find the volume of the tower.

subparts.stem: Sydney tower in Australia is the second tallest observation tower in the Southern Hemisphere. Find the volume of the tower.

mark_breakdown.desc: Determine the heights and radii of all four cylinders
Apply the cylinder volume formula $V = \pi r^2 h$ to sum the volumes
Correct total volume rounded appropriately to $14\,500\text{ m}^3$

subparts.solution:
$\text{Height of cylinder A} = 247\text{ m}$
$\text{Radius of cylinder A} = 3\text{ m}$

$\text{Height of cylinder B} = 258 - 247 = 11\text{ m}$
$\text{Radius of cylinder B} = \sqrt{6.94^2 + (-8.27)^2} = \sqrt{116.5565}\text{ m}$

$\text{Height of cylinder C} = 279 - 258 = 21\text{ m}$
$\text{Radius of cylinder C} = \sqrt{5.91^2 + 4.13^2} = \sqrt{51.985}\text{ m}$

$\text{Height of cylinder D} = 309 - 279 = 30\text{ m}$
$\text{Radius of cylinder D} = 0.6\text{ m}$

$\text{Volume of tower} = \text{volume of cylinder A} + \text{volume of cylinder B} + \text{volume of cylinder C} + \text{volume of cylinder D}$
$= \pi(3)^2 \times 247 + \pi(\sqrt{116.5565})^2 \times 11 + \pi(\sqrt{51.985})^2 \times 21 + \pi(0.6)^2 \times 30$
$= 2223\pi + 1282.1215\pi + 1091.685\pi + 10.8\pi$
$= 4607.6065\pi$
$\approx 14\,475.22$
$\approx 14\,500\text{ m}^3$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The volume of a right circular cylinder is given by $V = \pi r^2 h$. When a composite tower is formed by stacked cylinders, find each height from the difference in $z$-coordinates and each radius using the horizontal distance $\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$ from the central axis.
step_by_step: Find the height of each cylinder by subtracting consecutive z-coordinates.
Find the radius of each cylinder from the given $(x, y)$ coordinate: $r = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$.
Calculate each cylinder's volume using $V = \pi r^2 h$.
Sum the volumes to obtain the total volume and round to 3 significant figures.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to square the radius or using cumulative $z$-values instead of individual cylinder heights.
